reasoning: The document exhibits severe structural and visual defects, reflected in a very low structural fidelity score of 0.333. Multiple blockers for auto-approval are present, including duplicated content (tables rendered as both HTML and full-page screenshots), broken heading hierarchies, 97 retained header/footer elements, and displaced hyperlinks. Additionally, significant portions of the Table of Contents were omitted, requiring human remediation.

concerns.description: Significant text omission within a section
concerns.analysis: I compared the Table of Contents on page 2 of the source to the output. The source PDF contains a complete Table of Contents listing sections 1 through 5 and all Appendices. The JSON output for page 2 truncates the Table of Contents after Section 1.4.1 (Table 2). All entries for Sections 2, 3, 4, 5, and the Appendices are missing from the output list, representing a loss of more than 75% of the Table of Contents text.

The heading hierarchy is inconsistent across sibling sections. For instance, the section 'FY 2021 – 2022' is assigned H1 on page 31, while the sibling section 'FY 2022 – 2023' is assigned H2 on page 32. Furthermore, in the Appendix, 'Appendix A' on page 45 is rendered as H2 (nested under 'Appendix' H1), but 'Appendix B' on page 46 jumps back to an H1 level.

There are multiple instances of content duplication. First, the table of contents duplicates the 'Methodology' section completely. Second, the financial tables for FY 2021-2022 and FY 2022-2023 are rendered twice: once as HTML elements, and immediately again as full-page screenshot tags, forcing users to view the exact same content twice.

concerns.analysis: The source document uses bolding and underlining to emphasize terms like 'Goal 1:', 'Goal 2:', etc. in the Executive Summary. The HTML output strips this formatting and renders them as plain text list items.

concerns.analysis: Because the extraction merged tables across page breaks, it stripped entire pages of their main body content and shifted that content into the next page. Pages 35, 37, 39, and 41 in the output have no main content (only headers and footers), while their respective tables (Goal 3, 5, 7, 9) incorrectly appear sequentially after the header on the subsequent pages. This severely disrupts the reading flow relative to the original pagination.
